name: Rockchip Proximity Sensor
description: Read the vi530x time-of-flight proximity sensor found on some Rockchip panels. Publishes distance and near/far sensors to Home Assistant, fires gesture triggers when someone approaches or leaves and can wake the screen.
author: iiliev-nemetschek

settings.title: Near threshold
settings.description: Someone is near when the distance drops to this value or below.

settings.title: Far threshold
settings.description: Someone has left when the distance rises to this value or above. Keep it above the near threshold so the state does not flicker.

settings.title: Maximum reported distance
settings.description: Readings above this value are reported as this value. The sensor returns noisy, very large numbers when nothing is in front of it.

settings.title: Wake screen on approach
settings.description: Dismiss the screensaver and wake the display when the state changes from far to near.

settings.title: Expose to Home Assistant
settings.description: Adds a distance sensor and a near/far binary sensor to the kiosk ESPHome device and to the readings on this page. Turning it off removes both. Triggers and screen wake keep working.

settings.title: Minimum change to report
settings.description: The distance sensor updates only when the value moves by at least this much. Near/far changes are always reported.

settings.title: Minimum update interval
settings.description: The distance sensor updates at most this often. Near/far changes are always reported immediately.

settings.title: Allow root fallback
settings.description: Use a plugin helper through su only if direct access to the input device is denied. Your root manager may ask you to grant access.

settings.title: Simulation mode
settings.description: Sweep a fake distance without touching hardware. Home Assistant labels the sensors as simulated.
